translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to ascend the steps, descend from the dais, and thank for the banquet—as at the Empress Dowager's birthday.

sentences.zh: 冬至朝賀儀：臣僚班齊，如正旦儀。

translations.literal: Winter Solstice Court Congratulations Ceremony: Officials' ranks are assembled, as in the New Year's Day ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Solstice Court Congratulations Ceremony: Officials form their ranks as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后拜日，臣僚陪位再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress bow to the sun; officials in accompanying positions perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress bow to the sun; officials in accompanying positions bow twice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后升殿坐，契丹舍人通，臣僚入，合班，親王祝壽，宣答，皆如正旦之儀。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress ascend the hall and are seated; the Khitan chamberlain announces; officials enter; they unite ranks; the prince wishes long life; the response is proclaimed—all as in the New Year's Day ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress ascend the hall and take their seats; the Khitan chamberlain announces; officials enter and unite in rank; the prince wishes long life; the response is proclaimed—all as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 謝訖，舞蹈，五拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: When thanks are finished, dancing bow; five bows; bow with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: When thanks are finished, they perform the dancing bow with five bows and bow with body bent.

sentences.zh: 出班奏「聖躬萬福」；

translations.literal: They leave rank and report "May the sacred person enjoy ten thousand blessings";
translations.idiomatic: They leave formation and declare "May His Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings";

sentences.zh: 復位，再拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: return to position, perform a double bow, and bow with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: return to their places, bow twice, and bow with body bent.

sentences.zh: 班首出班，俯伏跪，祝壽訖，伏興，舞蹈，五拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The head of the rank leaves rank, prostrates and kneels, wishes long life; when finished, rises from prostration; dancing bow; five bows; bow with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the formation leaves rank, prostrates and kneels and wishes long life; when finished, he rises; he performs the dancing bow with five bows and bows with body bent.

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: "Each attend to duty" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to attend to their duties.

sentences.zh: 分班，不出，合班，御床入，再拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: They are dismissed by rank but do not go out; they unite ranks; the imperial couch enters; they perform a double bow and bow with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: They are dismissed by formation but do not withdraw; they unite in rank; the imperial couch is brought in; they bow twice and bow with body bent.

sentences.zh: 贊進酒。

translations.literal: "Present wine" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to present wine.

sentences.zh: 臣僚平身。

translations.literal: Officials stand with bodies level.
translations.idiomatic: Officials stand upright.

sentences.zh: 引親王左階上殿，就欄內褥位，搢笏，執臺盞，進酒。

translations.literal: A prince is led up the hall by the left steps to his cushion seat inside the railing; he tucks his tablet, holds a pedestal cup, and presents wine.
translations.idiomatic: A prince is led onto the dais by the left steps to his cushioned place inside the railing; he tucks his tablet, takes up a pedestal cup, and presents wine.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后受盞訖，退就褥位，置臺，出笏，俯伏跪。

translations.literal: When the emperor and empress have received the cups, he withdraws to his cushion seat, sets down the pedestal, withdraws his tablet, and prostrates kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and empress have received the cups, he withdraws to his cushioned place, sets down the pedestal, withdraws his tablet, and kneels prostrate.

sentences.zh: 少前，自通全銜臣某等謹進千萬歲壽酒。

translations.literal: He moves slightly forward and announces his full title himself: "Your servants such-and-such respectfully present wine for ten thousand years of longevity."
translations.idiomatic: He moves slightly forward and announces his full title: "Your servants such-and-such respectfully present wine for ten thousand years of longevity."

sentences.zh: 俯伏興，退，復褥位，再拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: He rises from prostration, withdraws, returns to his cushion seat, performs a double bow, and bows with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: He rises from prostration, withdraws to his cushioned place, bows twice, and bows with body bent.

sentences.zh: 殿下臣僚皆再拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: Officials below the hall all perform a double bow and bow with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: All officials below bow twice and bow with body bent.

sentences.zh: 宣答如正旦儀。

translations.literal: The proclaimed response is as in the New Year's Day ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The proclaimed response follows the New Year's Day ceremony.

sentences.zh: 親王搢笏，執臺，分班。

translations.literal: The prince tucks his tablet, holds the pedestal; they are dismissed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: The prince tucks his tablet and holds the pedestal; they are dismissed by formation.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后飲酒，奏樂；

translations.literal: The emperor and empress drink; music is played;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress drink; music is played;

sentences.zh: 殿上下臣僚皆拜，稱「萬歲壽」，樂止。

translations.literal: officials above and below the hall all bow and cry "Ten thousand years of longevity!"; music stops.
translations.idiomatic: all officials on and below the dais bow and exclaim "Ten thousand years of longevity!"; the music stops.

sentences.zh: 教坊再拜，臣僚合班。

translations.literal: The Music Office performs a double bow; officials unite ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office bows twice; officials unite in rank.

sentences.zh: 親王進受盞，至褥位，置臺盞，出笏，引左階下殿。

translations.literal: The prince advances to receive the cups, goes to his cushion seat, sets down the pedestal cups, withdraws his tablet, and is led down the hall by the left steps.
translations.idiomatic: The prince advances to receive the cups, goes to his cushioned place, sets down the pedestal cups, withdraws his tablet, and is led down from the dais by the left steps.

sentences.zh: 御床出。

translations.literal: The imperial couch is removed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial couch is removed.

sentences.zh: 親王復丹墀位，再拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The prince returns to the red-step position, performs a double bow, and bows with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: The prince returns to the red-step position, bows twice, and bows with body bent.

sentences.zh: 贊祗候。

translations.literal: "Attend to duty" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He is acclaimed to attend to his duty.

sentences.zh: 分班引出。

translations.literal: They are dismissed by rank and led out.
translations.idiomatic: They are dismissed by formation and led out.

sentences.zh: 班首右階上殿奏表目進奉。

translations.literal: The head of the rank ascends the hall by the right steps and reports the memorial lists and tribute presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the formation ascends the dais by the right steps to present the memorial lists and tribute.

sentences.zh: 諸道進奉，教坊進奉過訖，贊進奉收。

translations.literal: Tribute from all circuits and the Music Office's tribute presentation are finished; "Tribute received" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute from all circuits and the Music Office's presentation are finished, tribute receipt is proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 班首舞蹈，五拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The head of the rank performs the dancing bow with five bows and bows with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the formation performs the dancing bow with five bows and bows with body bent.

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: "Each attend to duty" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to attend to their duties.

sentences.zh: 班首出，臣僚復入，合班謝，舞蹈，五拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The head of the rank goes out; officials re-enter; they unite ranks and thank; dancing bow; five bows; bow with body bent.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the formation withdraws; officials re-enter; they unite in rank to thank; they perform the dancing bow with five bows and bow with body bent.

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: "Each attend to duty" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to attend to their duties.

sentences.zh: 分班引出。

translations.literal: They are dismissed by rank and led out.
translations.idiomatic: They are dismissed by formation and led out.

sentences.zh: 聲警，皇帝、皇后起，赴北殿。

translations.literal: The guard cry sounds; the emperor and empress rise and proceed to the northern hall.
translations.idiomatic: The guard cry sounds; the emperor and empress rise and proceed to the northern hall.

sentences.zh: 皇太后於御容殿，與皇帝、皇后率臣僚再拜。

translations.literal: At the Imperial Portrait Hall, the Empress Dowager together with the emperor and empress leads officials in a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Portrait Hall, the Empress Dowager together with the emperor and empress leads the officials in bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 皇太后上香，皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager offers incense; all perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager offers incense; all bow twice.

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: "Each attend to duty" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to attend to their duties.

sentences.zh: 可矮墩以上上殿。

translations.literal: Those of short-stool rank and above ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those of short-stool rank and above ascend the dais.

sentences.zh: 皇太后三進御容酒，陪位皆拜。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager presents wine to the imperial portrait three rounds; those in accompanying positions all bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager presents wine to the imperial portrait three times; those in accompanying positions all bow.

sentences.zh: 皇太后升殿坐。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ascends the hall and is seated.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ascends the hall and takes her seat.

sentences.zh: 皇帝就露臺上褥位，親王押北南臣僚班丹墀內立。

translations.literal: The emperor takes his cushion seat on the exposed terrace; a prince escorts the northern and southern officials' ranks to stand within the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor takes his cushioned place on the upper terrace; a prince escorts the northern and southern officials' formations to stand within the red steps.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再拜，臣僚皆拜，鞠躬，皇帝欄內跪，祝皇太后壽訖，復位，再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor performs a double bow; all officials bow and bow with bodies bent; the emperor kneels inside the railing and wishes the Empress Dowager long life; when finished, returns to position and performs a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bows twice; all officials bow and bow with bodies bent; the emperor kneels inside the railing and wishes the Empress Dowager long life; when finished, he returns to his place and bows twice.

sentences.zh: 凡拜，皆稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: At every bow they cry "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: At every bow they exclaim "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: "Each attend to duty" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to attend to their duties.

sentences.zh: 臣僚不出，皇帝、皇后側座，親王進酒，臣僚陪拜，皇太后宣答，皆如正旦之儀。

translations.literal: Officials do not go out; the emperor and empress sit to the side; a prince presents wine; officials bow in accompaniment; the Empress Dowager's response is proclaimed—all as in the New Year's Day ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Officials do not withdraw; the emperor and empress sit to one side; a prince presents wine; officials bow with them; the Empress Dowager's response is proclaimed—all as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 臣僚分班，不出，班首右階上殿奏表目，合班謝宣宴，上殿就位如儀。

translations.literal: Officials are dismissed by rank but do not go out; the head of the rank ascends the hall by the right steps and reports the memorial lists; they unite ranks and thank for the proclaimed banquet; they ascend the hall and take position as in the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are dismissed by formation but do not withdraw; the head of the formation ascends the dais by the right steps to present the memorial lists; they unite in rank to thank for the banquet and ascend to take their places as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 御床入。

translations.literal: The imperial couch is brought in.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial couch is brought in.

sentences.zh: 皇帝進皇太后酒如初，各就座行酒，宣飲盡，如皇太后生辰之儀。

translations.literal: The emperor presents wine to the Empress Dowager as at first; each takes a seat and wine is served; drinking finished is proclaimed—as in the Empress Dowager's birthday ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor presents wine to the Empress Dowager as before; each takes a seat and wine is served; when drinking is proclaimed finished, the proceedings follow the Empress Dowager's birthday ceremony.

sentences.zh: 皇后進酒，如皇帝之儀。

translations.literal: The empress presents wine, as in the emperor's ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The empress presents wine, as in the emperor's ceremony.

sentences.zh: 三進酒，行茶，教坊致語，行殽膳，大饌，七進酒。

translations.literal: Three rounds of wine; tea is served; the Music Office delivers formal address; dishes and full courses are served; the grand feast; seven rounds of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds of wine are presented; tea is served; the Music Office delivers the formal address; dishes and full courses are served; the grand feast is brought in; seven rounds of wine follow.

sentences.zh: 曲破，臣僚起，御床出，謝宴，皆如皇太后生辰儀。

translations.literal: At the suite break, officials rise; the imperial couch is removed; thanks for the banquet—all as in the Empress Dowager's birthday ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At the suite break, officials rise; the imperial couch is removed; thanks for the banquet—all as at the Empress Dowager's birthday.

sentences.zh: 立春儀：皇帝出就內殿，拜先帝御容，北南臣僚丹墀內合班，再拜。

translations.literal: Beginning of Spring Ceremony: The emperor goes out to the inner hall, bows to the late emperor's imperial portrait; northern and southern officials unite ranks within the red steps and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning of Spring Ceremony: The emperor goes to the inner hall and bows to the late emperor's portrait; northern and southern officials unite in rank within the red steps and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 可矮墩以上入殿，賜坐。

translations.literal: Those of short-stool rank and above enter the hall and are granted seats.
translations.idiomatic: Those of short-stool rank and above enter the hall and are granted seats.

sentences.zh: 帝進御容酒，陪位並侍立皆再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor presents wine to the imperial portrait; those in accompanying positions and those standing in attendance all perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor presents wine to the imperial portrait; those in accompanying positions and those standing in attendance all bow twice.

sentences.zh: 一進酒，臣僚下殿，左右相向立。

translations.literal: At the first round of wine, officials descend the hall and stand facing one another to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: At the first round of wine, officials descend from the dais and stand facing one another to left and right.

sentences.zh: 皇帝戴幡勝，等第賜幡勝。

translations.literal: The emperor wears a spring pennant; spring pennants are bestowed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wears a spring pennant; spring pennants are bestowed by rank.

sentences.zh: 臣僚簪畢，皇帝於土牛前上香，三奠酒，不拜。

translations.literal: When officials have finished pinning the pennants, the emperor before the clay ox offers incense and presents wine three times without bowing.
translations.idiomatic: When officials have finished pinning their pennants, the emperor offers incense before the clay ox and presents wine three times without bowing.

sentences.zh: 教坊動樂，侍儀使跪進彩杖。

translations.literal: The Music Office sets music in motion; the attendant protocol officer kneels and presents the colored staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office strikes up; the attendant protocol officer kneels and presents the colored staff.

sentences.zh: 皇帝鞭土牛，可矮墩以上北南臣僚丹墀內合班，跪左膝，受彩杖，直起，再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor flogs the clay ox; northern and southern officials of short-stool rank and above unite ranks within the red steps, kneel on the left knee, receive the colored staff, rise straight, and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flogs the clay ox; northern and southern officials of short-stool rank and above unite in rank within the red steps, kneel on the left knee, receive the colored staff, rise, and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: "Each attend to duty" is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They are acclaimed to attend to their duties.

sentences.zh: 司辰報春至，鞭土牛三匝矮墩鞭止，引節度使以上上殿，撒谷豆，擊土牛。

translations.literal: The timekeeper reports that spring has arrived; the clay ox is flogged three circuits and flogging stops at the short-stool rank; military commissioners and above are led up the hall; grain and beans are scattered; the clay ox is struck.
translations.idiomatic: The timekeeper announces that spring has arrived; the clay ox is flogged three circuits and flogging stops at the short-stool rank; military commissioners and above are led onto the dais; grain and beans are scattered; the clay ox is struck.

sentences.zh: 撒谷豆，許眾奪之。

translations.literal: Grain and beans are scattered; the multitude is permitted to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and beans are scattered; the crowd is permitted to seize them.

sentences.zh: 臣僚依位坐，酒兩行，春盤入。

translations.literal: Officials sit according to position; wine is presented two rounds; the spring platter enters.
translations.idiomatic: Officials sit according to their places; two rounds of wine are presented; the spring platter is brought in.

sentences.zh: 酒三行畢，行茶。

translations.literal: When three rounds of wine are finished, tea is served.
translations.idiomatic: When three rounds of wine are finished, tea is served.

sentences.zh: 皆起。

translations.literal: All rise.
translations.idiomatic: All rise.

sentences.zh: 禮畢。

translations.literal: The ceremony is finished.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony is finished.

sentences.zh: 重午儀：至日，臣僚昧爽赴禦帳，皇帝系長壽彩縷升車坐，引北南臣僚合班，如丹墀之儀。

translations.literal: Double Fifth Ceremony: On the day, officials at daybreak proceed to the imperial tent; the emperor ties on a longevity colored thread and ascends the carriage to be seated; northern and southern officials are led to unite ranks, as in the red-step ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Double Fifth Ceremony: On the appointed day, officials attend at daybreak at the imperial tent; the emperor ties on a longevity colored thread and mounts the carriage; northern and southern officials are led to unite in rank as at the red steps.

sentences.zh: 所司各賜壽縷，揖臣僚跪受，再拜。

translations.literal: The responsible offices each bestow longevity threads; officials are motioned to kneel and receive them and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices each bestow longevity threads; officials are motioned to kneel and receive them and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 引退，從駕至膳所，酒三行。

translations.literal: They are led to withdraw and follow the imperial procession to the dining quarters; wine is presented three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: They are led to withdraw and follow the imperial procession to the dining quarters; three rounds of wine are presented.

sentences.zh: 若賜宴，臨時聽敕。

translations.literal: If a banquet is bestowed, they await the edict at the time.
translations.idiomatic: If a banquet is bestowed, they await the edict at the time.

sentences.zh: 重九儀：北南臣僚旦赴禦帳，從駕至圍場，賜茶。

translations.literal: Double Ninth Ceremony: Northern and southern officials in the morning proceed to the imperial tent, follow the imperial procession to the hunting park, and are granted tea.
translations.idiomatic: Double Ninth Ceremony: Northern and southern officials attend the imperial tent in the morning, follow the imperial procession to the hunting park, and are granted tea.

sentences.zh: 皇帝就坐，引臣僚御前班立，所司各賜菊花酒，跪受，再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor takes his seat; officials are led to stand in formation before the throne; the responsible offices each bestow chrysanthemum wine; they kneel to receive it and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor takes his seat; officials are led to stand in formation before the throne; the responsible offices each bestow chrysanthemum wine; they kneel to receive it and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 酒三行，揖起。

translations.literal: Wine is presented three rounds; they are motioned to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds of wine are presented; they are motioned to rise.

sentences.zh: 藏鬮儀：至日，北南臣僚常服入朝，皇帝御天祥殿，臣僚依位賜坐。

translations.literal: Hidden-Lot Ceremony: On the day, northern and southern officials in ordinary dress enter court; the emperor presides in the Hall of Heavenly Felicity; officials are granted seats according to position.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden-Lot Ceremony: On the appointed day, northern and southern officials in ordinary dress attend court; the emperor presides in the Hall of Heavenly Felicity; officials are granted seats according to their places.

sentences.zh: 契丹南面，漢人北面，分朋行鬮，或五或七籌。

translations.literal: Khitan on the south, Han on the north; they divide into groups and draw lots, either five or seven tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan on the south and Han on the north divide into groups and draw lots, either five or seven tallies.

sentences.zh: 賜膳，入食畢，皆起。

translations.literal: A meal is bestowed; when eating is finished, all rise.
translations.idiomatic: A meal is bestowed; when they finish eating, all rise.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復坐行鬮如初。

translations.literal: After a short interval, they sit again and draw lots as at first.
translations.idiomatic: After a short interval, they sit again and draw lots as before.

sentences.zh: 晚賜茶，三籌或五籌，罷教坊承應。

translations.literal: In the evening tea is bestowed; three or five tallies; the Music Office's service is dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the evening tea is bestowed; three or five tallies; the Music Office's service is dismissed.

sentences.zh: 若帝得鬮，臣僚進酒訖，以次賜酒。

translations.literal: If the emperor draws the lot, when officials have finished presenting wine, wine is bestowed in order.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor draws the lot, after officials present wine, wine is bestowed in turn.

sentences.zh: 大康十年十二月二十二日，始行是儀。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the twelfth month of the tenth year of Dakang, this ceremony was first performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day of the twelfth month of the tenth year of Dakang, this ceremony was first performed.

sentences.zh: 是日不禦朝。

translations.literal: On that day the court is not held.
translations.idiomatic: On that day court is not held.

sentences.zh: 歲時雜儀：

translations.literal: Miscellaneous seasonal ceremonies:
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous seasonal ceremonies:

sentences.zh: 正旦，國俗以糯飯和白羊髓為餅，丸之若拳，每帳賜四十九枚。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, by national custom glutinous rice is mixed with white sheep marrow to make cakes rolled like fists; each tent is granted forty-nine pieces.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, by Khitan custom glutinous rice is mixed with white sheep marrow to make fist-sized cakes; each tent is granted forty-nine pieces.

sentences.zh: 戊夜，各於帳內窗中擲丸於外。

translations.literal: On the fifth watch of the night, each throws the balls out through the tent windows.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth watch of the night, each throws the balls out through the tent windows.

sentences.zh: 數偶，動樂，飲宴。

translations.literal: If the number is even, music is set in motion and there is feasting.
translations.idiomatic: If the count is even, music strikes up and there is feasting.

sentences.zh: 數奇，令巫十有二人鳴鈴，執箭，繞帳歌呼，帳內爆鹽壚中，燒地拍鼠，謂之驚鬼，居七日乃出。

translations.literal: If the number is odd, twelve shamans are ordered to ring bells and hold arrows, circling the tent singing and calling; inside the tent salt is exploded in a brazier and the ground is burned while rats are struck—this is called frightening ghosts; they remain inside seven days before going out.
translations.idiomatic: If the count is odd, twelve shamans ring bells and hold arrows, circling the tent singing and calling; inside the tent salt is exploded in a brazier and the ground is burned while rats are struck—this is called frightening away ghosts; they remain inside seven days before emerging.

sentences.zh: 國語謂正旦為「乃捏咿唲」。

translations.literal: In the national language New Year's Day is called "Nainieyi'er."
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language New Year's Day is called "Nainieyi'er."

sentences.zh: 「乃」，正也；

translations.literal: "Nai" means "correct";
translations.idiomatic: "Nai" means "correct";

sentences.zh: 捏咿唲，旦也。

translations.literal: "nieyi'er" means "daybreak."
translations.idiomatic: "nieyi'er" means "daybreak."

sentences.zh: 立春，婦人進春書，刻青繒為幟，像龍禦之；

translations.literal: At the beginning of spring, women present spring documents; blue silk is carved into pennants shaped like dragons to drive them;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of spring, women present spring documents; blue silk is carved into pennants shaped like dragons to drive them away;

sentences.zh: 或為蟾蜍，書幟曰「宜春」。

translations.literal: or they are made into toads, and the pennants are inscribed "May spring arrive."
translations.idiomatic: or they are made into toads, and the pennants are inscribed "May spring arrive."

sentences.zh: 人日，凡正月之日，一雞、二狗、三豕、四羊，五馬、六牛，七日為人。

translations.literal: Human Day: For the days of the first month—the first day is the chicken, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the horse, the sixth the ox, and the seventh day is for humans.
translations.idiomatic: Human Day: For the days of the first month—the first day is the chicken, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the horse, the sixth the ox, and the seventh day is for humans.

sentences.zh: 其占，晴為祥，陰為災。

translations.literal: In divination, clear weather is auspicious and overcast weather is calamitous.
translations.idiomatic: In divination, clear weather is auspicious and overcast weather portends misfortune.

sentences.zh: 俗煎餅食於庭中，謂之「薰天」。

translations.literal: By custom pancakes are fried and eaten in the courtyard; this is called "Smoking the Sky."
translations.idiomatic: By custom pancakes are fried and eaten in the courtyard; this is called "Smoking the Sky."

sentences.zh: 二月一日為中和節，國舅族蕭氏設宴，以延國族耶律氏，歲以為常。

translations.literal: The first day of the second month is the Mid-Harmony festival; the imperial maternal clan of the Xiao set a banquet to receive the imperial clan of the Yelü—this is annual custom.
translations.idiomatic: The first day of the second month is the Mid-Harmony festival; the imperial maternal clan of the Xiao host a banquet for the imperial clan of the Yelü—an annual custom.

sentences.zh: 國語是日為「𢘉裏叵」，「𢘉裏」，請也；

translations.literal: In the national language this day is called "Xiali Po"; "xiali" means "to invite";
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language this day is called "Xiali Po"; "xiali" means "to invite";

sentences.zh: 「叵」，時也。

translations.literal: "po" means "time."
translations.idiomatic: "po" means "time."

sentences.zh: 𢘉，讀若狎；

translations.literal: "Xia" is read like "xia" (familiar);
translations.idiomatic: "Xia" is pronounced like "xia" (familiar);

sentences.zh: 叵，讀若頗。

translations.literal: "po" is read like "po" (rather).
translations.idiomatic: "po" is pronounced like "po" (rather).

sentences.zh: 二月八日為悉達太子生辰，京府及諸州雕木為像，儀仗百戲導從，循城為樂。

translations.literal: The eighth day of the second month is the birthday of Prince Siddhartha; the capital prefecture and all circuits carve wooden images; ceremonial guards and a hundred entertainments lead the procession; they circle the city in celebration.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth day of the second month is the birthday of Prince Siddhartha; the capital and all circuits carve wooden images; ceremonial guards and a hundred entertainments lead the procession as they circle the city in celebration.

sentences.zh: 悉達太子者，西域凈梵王子，姓瞿曇氏，名釋迦牟尼。

translations.literal: Prince Siddhartha was a prince of pure Brahman lineage in the Western Regions, surnamed Gautama and named Shakyamuni.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Siddhartha was a prince of pure Brahman lineage in the Western Regions, of the Gautama clan, named Shakyamuni.

sentences.zh: 以其覺性，稱之曰「佛」。

translations.literal: Because of his awakened nature, he is called "Buddha."
translations.idiomatic: Because of his awakened nature, he is called "Buddha."

sentences.zh: 三月三日為上巳，國俗，刻木為兔，分朋走馬射之。

translations.literal: The third day of the third month is the Shangsi festival; by national custom wood is carved into rabbits; groups divide and ride horses shooting at them.
translations.idiomatic: The third day of the third month is the Shangsi festival; by Khitan custom wood is carved into rabbits; groups divide and ride horses shooting at them.

sentences.zh: 先中者勝，負朋下馬列跪進酒，勝朋馬上飲之。

translations.literal: Whoever hits first wins; the losing group dismounts, lines up kneeling, and presents wine; the winning group drinks on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever hits first wins; the losing group dismounts, lines up kneeling, and presents wine; the winning group drinks on horseback.

sentences.zh: 國語謂是日為「陶裏樺」。

translations.literal: In the national language this day is called "Taoli Hua."
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language this day is called "Taoli Hua."

sentences.zh: 「陶裏」，兔也；

translations.literal: "Taoli" means "rabbit";
translations.idiomatic: "Taoli" means "rabbit";

sentences.zh: 「樺」射也。

translations.literal: "hua" means "to shoot."
translations.idiomatic: "hua" means "to shoot."

sentences.zh: 五月重五日，午時，采艾葉和綿著衣，七事以奉天子，北南臣僚各賜三事，君臣宴樂，渤海膳夫進艾騣。

translations.literal: On the double fifth of the fifth month, at the noon hour, mugwort leaves are gathered and mixed with cotton to be placed in garments—seven items to present to the Son of Heaven; northern and southern officials are each granted three items; ruler and ministers feast; a Bohai cook presents mugwort for the forelock.
translations.idiomatic: On the double fifth of the fifth month, at noon, mugwort leaves are gathered and mixed with cotton for garments—seven items to present to the Son of Heaven; northern and southern officials are each granted three; ruler and ministers feast; a Bohai cook presents mugwort for the forelock.

sentences.zh: 以五彩絲為索纏臂，謂之「合歡結」。

translations.literal: With five-colored silk cords wound around the arms, this is called the "Union-of-Joy Knot."
translations.idiomatic: With five-colored silk cords wound around the arms, this is called the "Union-of-Joy Knot."

sentences.zh: 又以彩絲宛轉為人形簪之，謂之「長命縷」。

translations.literal: Colored silk is also twisted into human shapes and pinned in the hair; this is called the "Long-Life Thread."
translations.idiomatic: Colored silk is also twisted into human shapes and pinned in the hair; this is called the "Long-Life Thread."

sentences.zh: 國語謂是日為「討賽咿兒」。

translations.literal: In the national language this day is called "Tao Saiyi'er."
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language this day is called "Tao Saiyi'er."

sentences.zh: 「討」五；

translations.literal: "Tao" means "five";
translations.idiomatic: "Tao" means "five";

sentences.zh: 「賽咿兒」，月也。

translations.literal: "saiyi'er" means "month."
translations.idiomatic: "saiyi'er" means "month."

sentences.zh: 夏至之日，俗謂之「朝節」。

translations.literal: On the day of the summer solstice, by custom it is called the "Court Festival."
translations.idiomatic: On the summer solstice, by custom it is called the "Court Festival."

sentences.zh: 婦人進彩扇，以粉脂囊相贈遺。

translations.literal: Women present colored fans and give one another powder and cosmetic pouches as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Women present colored fans and exchange powder and cosmetic pouches as gifts.

sentences.zh: 六月十有八日，國俗，耶律氏設宴，以延國舅族蕭氏，亦謂之「𢘉裏叵」

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the sixth month, by national custom the Yelü clan set a banquet to receive the imperial maternal clan of the Xiao; it is also called "Xiali Po."
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the sixth month, by Khitan custom the Yelü clan host a banquet for the imperial maternal clan of the Xiao; it is also called "Xiali Po."

sentences.zh: 七月十三日，夜，天子於宮西三十里卓帳宿焉。

translations.literal: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month, the Son of Heaven pitches a tent and lodges thirty li west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month, the Son of Heaven pitches a tent and lodges thirty li west of the palace.

sentences.zh: 前期，備酒饌。

translations.literal: Beforehand, wine and food are prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand, wine and food are prepared.

sentences.zh: 翼日，諸軍部落從者皆動蕃樂，飲宴至暮，乃歸行宮，謂之「迎節」。

translations.literal: The next day, all armies and tribal followers set Khitan music in motion and feast until evening; then they return to the traveling palace—this is called "Welcoming the Festival."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, all armies and tribal followers strike up Khitan music and feast until evening; then they return to the traveling palace—this is called "Welcoming the Festival."

sentences.zh: 十五日中元，動漢樂，大宴。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth, the Zhongyuan festival; Han music is set in motion and there is a great banquet.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth is the Zhongyuan festival; Han music strikes up and there is a great banquet.

sentences.zh: 十六日昧爽，復往西方，隨行諸軍部落大噪三，謂之「送節」。

translations.literal: At daybreak on the sixteenth they again proceed westward; the armies and tribes following raise a great clamor three times—this is called "Sending Off the Festival."
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak on the sixteenth they again proceed westward; the armies and tribes following raise a great clamor three times—this is called "Sending Off the Festival."

sentences.zh: 國語謂之「賽咿兒奢」。

translations.literal: In the national language it is called "Saiyi'er She."
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language it is called "Saiyi'er She."

sentences.zh: 「奢」，好也。

translations.literal: "She" means "good."
translations.idiomatic: "She" means "good."

sentences.zh: 八月八日，國俗，屠白犬，於寢帳前七步瘞之，露其喙。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the eighth month, by national custom a white dog is slaughtered and buried seven paces before the sleeping tent, its snout exposed.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the eighth month, by Khitan custom a white dog is slaughtered and buried seven paces before the sleeping tent, its snout exposed.

sentences.zh: 後七日中秋，移寢帳於其上。

translations.literal: Seven days later at the Mid-Autumn festival, the sleeping tent is moved above it.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later at Mid-Autumn, the sleeping tent is moved above it.

sentences.zh: 國語謂之「捏褐耐」。

translations.literal: In the national language it is called "Niehe Nai."
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language it is called "Niehe Nai."

sentences.zh: 「捏褐」，犬也；

translations.literal: "Niehe" means "dog";
translations.idiomatic: "Niehe" means "dog";

sentences.zh: 「耐」，首也。

translations.literal: "nai" means "head."
translations.idiomatic: "nai" means "head."

sentences.zh: 九月重九日，天子率群臣部族射虎，少者為負，罰重九宴。

translations.literal: On the double ninth of the ninth month, the Son of Heaven leads ministers, officials, and tribes to shoot tigers; whoever takes fewer is the loser and is fined a Double Ninth banquet.
translations.idiomatic: On the double ninth of the ninth month, the Son of Heaven leads ministers, officials, and tribes to shoot tigers; whoever takes fewer loses and must pay for a Double Ninth banquet.

sentences.zh: 射畢，擇高地卓帳，賜蕃、漢臣僚飲菊花酒。

translations.literal: When shooting is finished, a high place is chosen to pitch a tent; Khitan and Han officials are granted chrysanthemum wine.
translations.idiomatic: When shooting is finished, a high place is chosen to pitch a tent; Khitan and Han officials are granted chrysanthemum wine.

sentences.zh: 兔肝為臡，鹿舌為醬，又研茱萸酒，灑門戶以禬禳。

translations.literal: Rabbit liver serves as relish, deer tongue as sauce; cornelian cherry wine is also prepared and sprinkled on doors and gates for exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: Rabbit liver serves as relish and deer tongue as sauce; cornelian cherry wine is also prepared and sprinkled on doors and gates for exorcism.

sentences.zh: 國語謂是日為「必裏遲離」，九月九日也。

translations.literal: In the national language this day is called "Bili Chili"—the ninth day of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language this day is called "Bili Chili"—the ninth day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 歲十月，五京進紙造小衣甲、槍刀、器械萬副。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the year, the five capitals present paper-made small garments, armor, spears, blades, and ten thousand sets of equipment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the year, the five capitals present paper-made small garments, armor, spears, blades, and ten thousand sets of equipment.

sentences.zh: 十五日，天子與群臣望祭木葉山，用國字書狀，並焚之。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth, the Son of Heaven with his ministers performs a distant sacrifice toward Muye Mountain; documents are written in the national script and all are burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth, the Son of Heaven and his ministers perform a distant sacrifice toward Muye Mountain; documents are written in the Khitan script and burned.

sentences.zh: 國語謂之「戴辣」。

translations.literal: In the national language it is called "Dai La."
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language it is called "Dai La."

sentences.zh: 「戴」，燒也；

translations.literal: "Dai" means "to burn";
translations.idiomatic: "Dai" means "to burn";

sentences.zh: 「辣」，甲也。

translations.literal: "la" means "armor."
translations.idiomatic: "la" means "armor."

sentences.zh: 冬至日，國俗，屠白羊、白馬、白雁，各取血和酒，天子望拜黑山。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice, by national custom white sheep, white horses, and white geese are slaughtered; blood from each is mixed with wine; the Son of Heaven performs a distant bow toward Black Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice, by Khitan custom white sheep, white horses, and white geese are slaughtered; blood from each is mixed with wine; the Son of Heaven performs a distant bow toward Black Mountain.

sentences.zh: 黑山在境北，俗謂國人魂魄，其神司之，猶中國之岱宗雲。

translations.literal: Black Mountain is in the northern borderlands; by custom it is said to be where the people's souls reside and its spirit presides over them—like Mount Dai of China.
translations.idiomatic: Black Mountain lies in the northern borderlands; by custom it is said to be where the people's souls reside and its spirit presides over them—like Mount Tai of China.

sentences.zh: 每歲是日，五京進紙造人馬萬餘事，祭山而焚之。

translations.literal: Every year on this day, the five capitals present more than ten thousand paper-made human figures and horses; they sacrifice to the mountain and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Every year on this day, the five capitals present more than ten thousand paper-made human figures and horses; they sacrifice to the mountain and burn them.

sentences.zh: 俗甚嚴畏，非祭不敢近山。

translations.literal: By custom there is great dread; without sacrifice one dare not approach the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: By custom there is great dread; without sacrifice one dare not approach the mountain.

sentences.zh: 臘辰日：天子率北南臣僚並戎服，戊夜坐朝，作樂飲酒，等第賜甲仗、羊馬。

translations.literal: La Festival Day: The Son of Heaven leads northern and southern officials all in military dress; on the fifth watch of the night they hold court seated, set music and drink wine, and bestow armor, weapons, sheep, and horses by rank.
translations.idiomatic: La Festival Day: The Son of Heaven leads northern and southern officials all in military dress; on the fifth watch of the night they hold seated court, strike up music and drink wine, and bestow armor, weapons, sheep, and horses by rank.

sentences.zh: 國語謂是日為「炒伍侕叵」。

translations.literal: In the national language this day is called "Chao Wuer Po."
translations.idiomatic: In the Khitan language this day is called "Chao Wuer Po."

sentences.zh: 「炒伍侕」，戰也。

translations.literal: "Chao Wuer" means "battle."
translations.idiomatic: "Chao Wuer" means "battle."

sentences.zh: 再生儀：凡十有二歲，皇帝本命前一年季冬之月，擇吉日。

translations.literal: Rebirth Ceremony: At twelve years of age, in the last month of winter in the year before the emperor's birth year, an auspicious day is chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Rebirth Ceremony: At twelve years of age, in the last month of winter in the year before the emperor's birth year, an auspicious day is chosen.

sentences.zh: 前期，禁門北除地置再生室、母後室、先帝神主輿。

translations.literal: Beforehand, ground is cleared north of the forbidden gate to set up the Rebirth Chamber, the Mother's Chamber, and the late emperor's spirit tablet carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand, ground is cleared north of the forbidden gate to set up the Rebirth Chamber, the Mother's Chamber, and the late emperor's spirit tablet carriage.

sentences.zh: 在再生室東南，倒植三岐木。

translations.literal: Southeast of the Rebirth Chamber, a three-forked tree is planted upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the Rebirth Chamber, a three-forked tree is planted upside down.

sentences.zh: 其日，以童子及產醫嫗置室中，一婦人執酒，一叟持矢箙，立於室外。

translations.literal: On the day, boys and midwives are placed in the chamber; one woman holds wine, one old man holds a quiver of arrows, and they stand outside the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On the day, boys and midwives are placed in the chamber; one woman holds wine, one old man holds a quiver of arrows, and they stand outside the chamber.

sentences.zh: 有司請神主降輿，致奠。

translations.literal: The responsible offices request that the spirit tablet descend from its carriage and offerings be presented.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices request that the spirit tablet descend from its carriage and offerings be presented.

sentences.zh: 奠訖，皇帝出寢殿，詣再生室。

translations.literal: When the offerings are finished, the emperor leaves the sleeping hall and proceeds to the Rebirth Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When the offerings are finished, the emperor leaves the sleeping hall and proceeds to the Rebirth Chamber.

sentences.zh: 群臣奉迎，再拜。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers escort him in welcome; they perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers escort him in welcome and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入室。

translations.literal: The emperor enters the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enters the chamber.

sentences.zh: 釋服、洗。

translations.literal: He removes his ceremonial dress and washes.
translations.idiomatic: He removes his ceremonial dress and washes.

sentences.zh: 以童子從，三過岐木之下。

translations.literal: Accompanied by boys, he passes three times beneath the forked tree.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanied by boys, he passes three times beneath the forked tree.

sentences.zh: 每過，產醫嫗致詞，拂拭帝躬。

translations.literal: At each passing, the midwives deliver words of address and brush the emperor's person.
translations.idiomatic: At each passing, the midwives speak formal words and brush the emperor's body.

sentences.zh: 童子過岐木七，皇帝臥木側，叟擊箙曰：「生男矣。

translations.literal: The boys pass the forked tree seven times; the emperor lies beside the tree; the old man strikes the quiver and says: "A boy has been born."
translations.idiomatic: The boys pass the forked tree seven times; the emperor lies beside the tree; the old man strikes the quiver and announces: "A boy has been born."

sentences.zh: 」太巫幪皇帝首，興，群臣稱賀，再拜。

translations.literal: " The grand shaman covers the emperor's head; he rises; the assembled ministers offer congratulations and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: " The grand shaman covers the emperor's head; he rises; the assembled ministers offer congratulations and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 產醫嫗受酒於執酒婦以進，太巫奉繈褓、彩結等物贊祝之。

translations.literal: The midwives receive wine from the woman holding wine and present it; the grand shaman holds swaddling clothes, colored knots, and other objects and proclaims blessings over them.
translations.idiomatic: The midwives receive wine from the woman holding wine and present it; the grand shaman holds swaddling clothes, colored knots, and other objects and proclaims blessings over them.

sentences.zh: 預選七叟，各立御名系於彩，皆跪進。

translations.literal: Seven old men are chosen beforehand; each attaches an imperial name to colored silk and all kneel to present them.
translations.idiomatic: Seven old men are chosen beforehand; each attaches an imperial name to colored silk and all kneel to present them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝選嘉名受之，賜物。

translations.literal: The emperor selects an auspicious name and receives it; gifts are bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor selects an auspicious name and receives it; gifts are bestowed.

sentences.zh: 再拜，退。

translations.literal: He performs a double bow and withdraws.
translations.idiomatic: He bows twice and withdraws.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆進繈褓、彩結等物。

translations.literal: All ministers present swaddling clothes, colored knots, and other objects.
translations.idiomatic: All ministers present swaddling clothes, colored knots, and other objects.

sentences.zh: 皇帝拜先帝諸御容，遂宴群臣。

translations.literal: The emperor bows to the late emperor's various imperial portraits, then feasts the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bows to the late emperor's various portraits, then feasts the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 善哉，阻午可汗之垂訓後嗣也。

translations.literal: Excellent! This is Zuwu Khan's instruction handed down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent! This is the legacy Zuwu Khan bequeathed to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 孺子無不慕其親者，嗜欲深而愛淺，妻子具而孝衰。

translations.literal: No child fails to yearn for his parents, yet when desires grow deep love grows shallow, and when wife and children are complete filial piety declines.
translations.idiomatic: Every child yearns for his parents, yet when desires grow deep love grows shallow, and when wife and children are complete filial piety declines.

sentences.zh: 人人皆然，而況天子乎！

translations.literal: This is true of everyone—how much more so the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: This is true of everyone—how much more so the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 再生之儀，歲一周星，使天子一行是禮，以起其孝心。

translations.literal: The Rebirth Ceremony, once each year as a star completes its circuit, causes the Son of Heaven to perform this rite in order to awaken his filial heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Rebirth Ceremony, performed once each year as the stars complete their circuit, requires the Son of Heaven to perform this rite in order to awaken his filial heart.

sentences.zh: 夫體之也真，則其思之也切，孺子之慕，將有油然發於中心者，感發之妙，非言語文字之所能及。

translations.literal: When the embodiment is genuine, then the thought is keen; the child's yearning will well up spontaneously from the center of the heart—the subtlety of stirring the feelings is beyond what words and writing can reach.
translations.idiomatic: When the enactment is genuine, the remembrance is keen; a child's yearning will well up spontaneously from the heart—the power of stirring feeling is beyond what words and writing can convey.

sentences.zh: 善哉，阻午可汗之垂訓後嗣也。

translations.literal: Excellent! This is Zuwu Khan's instruction handed down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent! This is the legacy Zuwu Khan bequeathed to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 始之以三過岐木，母氏劬勞能無念乎！

translations.literal: It begins with passing three times beneath the forked tree—can one fail to recall the mother's toil!
translations.idiomatic: It begins with passing three times beneath the forked tree—who could fail to recall a mother's toil!

sentences.zh: 終之以拜先帝御容，敬承宗廟宜何如哉！

translations.literal: It ends with bowing to the late emperor's imperial portraits—how fitting to reverently uphold the ancestral temple!
translations.idiomatic: It ends with bowing to the late emperor's portraits—how fitting to reverently uphold the ancestral temple!

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「無念爾祖，聿修厥德。」

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Do not fix your thoughts on your ancestors alone; cultivate their virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "Do not merely think of your ancestors; cultivate their virtue."
